```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load your data here
sample_submission <- read_csv("data/sample_submission.csv")
test <- read_csv("data/test.csv")
train <- read_csv("data/train.csv")

train <- train %>%
  select(Id,OverallQual,GrLivArea,YearBuilt,Neighborhood,MSZoning,LotFrontage,SalePrice)

train <- train %>%
  mutate(OverallQual = case_when(
    OverallQual > 7 ~ "High Qual",
    OverallQual < 4 ~ "Low Qual",
    OverallQual > 3 & OverallQual < 8  ~ "Med Qual"))

train <- train %>%
  mutate(
  OverallQual = fct_relevel(as.factor(OverallQual), "Low Qual", "Med Qual", "High Qual"))

test <- test %>%
 select(Id,OverallQual,GrLivArea,YearBuilt,Neighborhood,MSZoning,LotFrontage)

test <- test %>%
  mutate(OverallQual = case_when(
    OverallQual > 7 ~ "High Qual",
    OverallQual < 4 ~ "Low Qual",
    OverallQual > 3 & OverallQual < 8  ~ "Med Qual"))
```

# Data Overview:

Our project uses three related datasets derived from the Ames Housing data. After cleaning the data we selected our variables and split them into two groups, Group A (House Features) and Group B (Location Variables).

We engineered two new variables:

log_saleprice — the natural log of SalePrice to reduce skew and support linear modelling

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.show='hold', out.width='48%'}

train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    # log-transform target
    log_saleprice = log(SalePrice),)

# Original SalePrice
ggplot(train, aes(x = SalePrice)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of SalePrice")

# Log-transformed SalePrice
ggplot(train, aes(x = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of log(SalePrice)")


```
---

Mag_Price — a binary classification (“High” / “Low”) indicating whether a home’s log-price is above or below the training-set mean

We also recoded OverallQual into three descriptive quality categories (“Low”, “Med”, “High”) for clearer interpretation.

To support our comparison of house features vs. location factors, we retained the following predictors:

House-related variables: OverallQual, GrLivArea, YearBuilt

Location-related variables: Neighborhood, MSZoning, LotFrontage
```{r, echo=FALSE}

library(knitr)

data.frame(
  Variable = c(
    # Group A — House Features
    "OverallQual", "GrLivArea", "YearBuilt",
    
    # Group B — Location Features
    "Neighborhood", "MSZoning", "LotFrontage",
    
    # Engineered Variables
    "log_saleprice", "Mag_Price"
  ),
  
  Type = c(
    # Group A
    "Categorical",
    "Numeric",
    "Numeric",
    
    # Group B
    "Categorical",
    "Categorical",
    "Numeric",
    
    # Engineered
    "Numeric",
    "Categorical"
  ),
  
  Description = c(
    # Group A descriptions
    "Reclassified overall finish and quality of the home",
    "Living area in square feet",
    "Year the house was originally built",
    
    # Group B descriptions
    "Residential neighborhood where the home is located",
    "Zoning classification for land use",
    "Linear feet of street-connected property frontage",
    
    # Engineered variable descriptions
    "Natural log transformation of SalePrice to reduce skew",
    "Binary label of log_saleprice"
  )
) %>%
  kable()

```

### Group A (House Features)

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.show='hold', out.width='32%'}

  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +

  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +

    title = "log(SalePrice) vs Year Built",
    x = "Year Built",
    y = "log(SalePrice)"
  )
```

ggplot(train, aes(x = LotFrontage, y = log_saleprice)) +

  theme_minimal() +

    title = "log(SalePrice) vs Lot Frontage",
    x = "LotFrontage (linear feet)",

# Tables


```{r include=FALSE}
sample_submission <- read_csv("data/sample_submission.csv")
test <- read_csv("data/test.csv")
train <- read_csv("data/train.csv")
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    # log-transform target
    log_saleprice = log(SalePrice),
  )
train <- train %>%
 mutate(log_avg_price = mean(log_saleprice))

sample_submission <- sample_submission %>%
 mutate(log_saleprice = log(SalePrice))

sample_submission <- sample_submission %>%
 mutate(log_avg_price = mean(log_saleprice))

train <- train %>%
  mutate(Mag_Price = case_when(
    log_saleprice > log_avg_price ~ "High",
    log_saleprice < log_avg_price ~ "Low"),
    Mag_Price = fct_relevel(Mag_Price, "Low", "High"))

sample_submission <- sample_submission %>%
  mutate(Mag_Price = case_when(
    log_saleprice > log_avg_price ~ "High",
    log_saleprice < log_avg_price ~ "Low"),
    Mag_Price = fct_relevel(Mag_Price, "Low", "High"))
train_rec_2 <- recipe(
  Mag_Price ~ GrLivArea + OverallQual + YearBuilt,
  data = train) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
train_mod_2 <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm")
train_wflow_2 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(train_mod_2) %>%
  add_recipe(train_rec_2)
train_fit_2 <- train_wflow_2 %>%
  fit(data = train)
tidy(train_fit_2)
train_test_2 <- predict(train_fit_2, test, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(sample_submission )
glimpse(train_test_2)
roc <- roc_curve(
  train_test_2,
  truth = Mag_Price,
  .pred_High,
  event_level = "second"
)
autoplot(roc)
roc_auc(
  train_test_2,
  truth = Mag_Price,
  .pred_High,
  event_level = "second"
)
```

Log_saleprice = -100.93 + 0.0039 * GrLivArea + 1.060 * OverallQual + 0.045 * YearBuilt
- Made this a logistic value, as we have mutated the log_saleprice into a categorical variable for a better visual representation of our prediction.
- We limited the amount of variables in our regression model to prevent overfitting.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
df <- tidy(train_fit_2)
kable(df, format = "html")
```

---
# Table 2
- Trained logistic model where we mutated Magnitude of Price as high and low for log_saleprice is greater or less than mean(log_saleprice) respectively.
- Settled with using LotFrontage, Neighborhood and MSZoning as our explanatory variables.
- The ROC curve gave an AUC value of 0.686, which implies a below average predictive power. This suggests that the model tends to give a slightly higher predicted probability for sale prices that are greater than the mean.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
roc <- roc_curve(
  train_test_2,
  truth = Mag_Price,
  .pred_High,
  event_level = "second"
)
autoplot(roc)
roc_auc(
  train_test_2,
  truth = Mag_Price,
  .pred_High,
  event_level = "second"
)
```

You can write LaTeX math expressions inside a pair of dollar signs, e.g. &#36;\alpha+\beta$ renders $\alpha+\beta$. You can use the display style with double dollar signs:

Limitations:

1. The source code of a LaTeX math expression must be in one line, unless it is inside a pair of double dollar signs, in which case the starting `$$` must appear in the very beginning of a line, followed immediately by a non-space character, and the ending `$$` must be at the end of a line, led by a non-space character;

1. There should not be spaces after the opening `$` or before the closing `$`.
